clue.text: Odd coin (in part of orient, mainly) depicting shrub

indicators.note: a picture that is depicting something holds it within its frame, so one piece goes inside the other
mainly means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: Japan is a country in the Orient, the Far East

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange coin from somewhere in the Far East shows a picture of a shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed aside is wordplay, not scenery: 'part of orient, mainly' is a country with its last letter cut, and 'depicting' means holding the jumbled coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Japonica is the Japanese quince, a flowering garden bush.

clue.text: James 'Suavity 'Bond

parts.note: J is the standard abbreviation of the name James
unction is an oily, smooth manner of speech, a show of suavity

explanation.surface: It reads like a nickname: James 'Suavity' Bond, the smooth secret agent.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the fictional spy; here 'Bond' is a common noun meaning a joining or link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond is a connection or joint, the place where two things meet and join.

clue.text: Deck with silver and eastern wrap

parts.note: a deck of cards is also called a pack
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A card deck is wrapped up with silver and oriental trimmings.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrapped parcel is a bundle sent through the post.

clue.text: Group in advance promoted records

indicators.note: promoted means moved up, and in a down entry moving up means reading the letters bottom to top

parts.note: a set is a group of things
on can mean ahead or forward, as in 'getting on'

explanation.surface: A team moving ahead earns promotion on the strength of its records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoted' turns the whole run SETON upwards, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes are written records, jottings made to remember something.

clue.text: Focus is of the essence

definitions.meaning: to focus is to direct all one's attention
a reduced, essential form of a juice or liquid, its strongest extract

explanation.surface: Focus, because it is vitally important.
explanation.definitionFit: To focus is to fix one's mind hard; a juice reduced to its essence is a strong extract of the same name.

clue.text: Manages to track sun, having optical instruments

indicators.note: to track something is to follow behind it, so this piece comes after the sun

parts.note: copes means manages or gets by

explanation.surface: Someone succeeds in following the sun's path with telescopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Telescopes, microscopes and periscopes are all viewing devices.

clue.text: Sign of farm produce on island

indicators.note: on here means placed next to, attaching the produce to the island

parts.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
corn is a crop grown on farms

explanation.surface: A sign that farm crops are grown on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricorn is the tenth sign of the zodiac, the goat.

clue.text: Dissemble before minister

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
to minister to someone is to tend them

explanation.surface: Someone tells lies in front of a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissemble is to put on a false show, to fake.

clue.text: Force ultimately cracks lock

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: Enough force in the end breaks open a lock.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is pressure or strain applied to something.

clue.text: Drug as tonic synthesised in east

indicators.note: synthesised means made up from parts, so the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A drug made as a tonic in a laboratory in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is only a link; read 'in east' as the word IN beside E, not as a container instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicotine is the addictive stimulant found in tobacco.

clue.text: Show up a fellow by word of mouth

indicators.note: word of mouth means spoken, so the letters entered are what the words sound like

parts.note: a gives A; a peer is a fellow or equal, one of the same rank

explanation.surface: A man turns up having heard about it by word of mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: To show up is to arrive or become visible.

clue.text: Vehicles making sharp turn

indicators.note: to turn the word is to read it backwards

parts.note: smart means sharp, clever or quick-witted

explanation.surface: Vehicles take a sharp bend.
explanation.definitionFit: Trams are passenger carriages running on street rails.

clue.text: Result of vacation in Spain, wildly misspent

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

indicators.note: wildly signals the letters of the next word are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A holiday in Spain spent recklessly leaves an empty wallet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' is not a holiday here but the act of vacating or emptying; 'wildly' rearranges MISSPENT to follow E.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacating a place leaves it empty, so the outcome is a void.

clue.text: Smart host, being well up to it

parts.note: to host a television show is to present it
able means capable, well up to a task

explanation.surface: An elegant host who is perfectly capable.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart and presentable both describe someone looking neat and fit to be seen.

clue.text: A saloon might provide this in more senses than one

definitions.text: A saloon might provide this in more senses than one

parts.words: A saloon might provide this in more senses than one
parts.note: a saloon is both a bar, which serves a last drink before leaving, and a car, which takes you along the highway

explanation.surface: A bar or a car can each offer it.
explanation.walkthrough: A saloon bar serves a final drink before setting off, while a saloon car is literally built for the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a parting drink, and literally describes a car meant for travel.

clue.text: Cards (masters)

definitions.meaning: a card is an eccentric or amusing character
master copies, first versions from which copies are made

explanation.definitionFit: Eccentric people and the first versions of artworks or documents both go by this word.

clue.text: Yorkshire river, flooding fissures, presents hazards

indicators.note: a river flooding a crack fills it, so the river goes inside the fissures

parts.note: vents are openings or cracks
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: A river in Yorkshire pours into cracks and creates dangers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hazards' is a verb (risks), not a noun, so it matches the answer as a verb; 'presents' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To hazard is to risk or dare, as one dares an opinion.

clue.text: Soldier's pay?

parts.note: a private is an ordinary soldier, so the wages of a private would be his income

explanation.surface: What does an army man earn?
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means unearned money from investments, but read literally it is the earnings of an army private.
explanation.definitionFit: Unearned money from investments or inheritance is the real meaning; a ranker's wages is the literal one.

clue.text: Roof piece for stack cut by worker

indicators.note: a word cut by another is split open with the other placed inside

parts.note: a pile is a stack
a worker ant is a classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A roofing component for a heap is sliced by a labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantile is a curved S-shaped tile used on roofs.

clue.text: Veteran soldier-one yielding to time, maybe

indicators.note: maybe signals that the letters may be arranged differently
one thing yielding to another gives way to it, so one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An old soldier gives way to the march of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yielding to' replaces the I of SOLDIER with T, making SOLDTER, and 'maybe' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldster is an elderly person, an old hand.

clue.text: Car parking found after climbing south-eastern rock face

indicators.note: climbing means going up, so in a down entry the letters read upward

parts.note: taken as written
P is the map symbol for parking

explanation.surface: A car park is found after a climb up a south-eastern cliff.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'climbing' reads upward, and 'found after' puts the car and parking behind that reversed compass pair.
explanation.definitionFit: An escarp is a steep slope or cliff, an escarpment.

clue.text: Attitude aroused about New Age

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: sent can mean thrilled or roused, as in music that sends you
an age is a time or era

explanation.surface: An attitude stirred up by New Age ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentiment is a view or feeling about something.

clue.text: Officer in the making acted as ordered

indicators.note: as ordered means arranged into order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trainee officer obeys commands.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a trainee at a military academy, a future officer.

clue.text: Intensive search after cold chisel

indicators.note: after means the search comes behind the cold

parts.note: heat is slang for intense police pursuit

explanation.surface: A tool hunted for hard after a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chisel' is slang for swindle, not the carpenter's tool.
explanation.definitionFit: To chisel someone is slang for swindling them out of money.

clue.text: Creature identified by rounded scale

indicators.note: rounded means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a lamina is a thin scale or layer

explanation.surface: A beast recognised by its round scales.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal is any living creature that is not a plant.

clue.text: Who takes a stand, sighting gold on target?

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the gold follows the target

parts.note: an object is an aim or target
or is heraldic gold

explanation.surface: An archer sights gold on the target and takes a stand.
explanation.walkthrough: The gold here is not the bullseye but OR, gold in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: An objector protests, taking up a position against something.

clue.text: Content with suit bridge players

parts.note: a suit in law is a plea or petition
S and E, South and East, are two of the four players at bridge

explanation.surface: A satisfied pair at the bridge table follow suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' is a verb here, to satisfy.
explanation.definitionFit: To content someone is to satisfy them.

clue.text: Renovates support with rambling rose attached

parts.note: a rest is a support, as in an armrest

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about, so the letters of the flower wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener repairs a trellis with a rambling rose tied on.
explanation.definitionFit: To renovate a building is to bring it back to good condition.
